decision.summary: The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point to combat high inflation.

changes.quote: The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.
changes.explanation: The Fed is resuming rate hikes to ensure inflation continues to fall toward its target.

changes.quote: While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient.
changes.explanation: Officials are noting that despite global risks, American consumers are still spending enough to keep the economy moving.
The Fed removed specific mentions of supply shocks to signal that inflation is now a broader problem.

changes.quote: Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.
changes.explanation: This new sentence explains that the rate hike is intended to speed up the process of lowering inflation.

changes.quote: Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust.
changes.explanation: The Fed upgraded its description of business investment to robust, suggesting the economy is handling higher rates well.

tone_quotes.quote: Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.
The Committee will deliver price stability.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 20.94% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.
Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate, and a 1 bp move in the 10-year yield would raise the monthly payment on a $300,000 loan at 6.71% by about $1.99.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 51k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: Core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The S&P 500 moved -0.45% on the day of the announcement.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.03% on the day.

card.whats_next: The Fed is signaling a more aggressive stance to bring inflation back to its 2 percent target. Future meetings will likely focus on whether today's hike is enough to ensure a timely return to price stability.
